## Short biography {#short-biography}

For introductions, programs and speaker notes.

<div class="bio-panel"><p id="short-bio">Md Bodrud-Doza is a Postdoctoral Scholar in the Department of Geography, Environment and Geomatics at the University of Guelph, Canada. His research combines watershed modelling, geospatial analysis and machine learning to identify where agricultural conservation practices can most improve water quality. He holds a PhD in Geography from the University of Guelph (2026) and has published widely on water quality, precision conservation and climate resilience. Before his doctorate he spent six years in climate-adaptation research and program management in Bangladesh with BRAC and the International Centre for Climate Change and Development.</p><button class="copy-button" type="button" data-copy-target="short-bio" hidden>Copy biography</button><span class="copy-status" role="status" aria-live="polite"></span></div>

## Research support and proposal development

The entries state my role in each case. I have not yet held a grant as principal investigator.

- **Current support · 2026–present:** Mitacs Accelerate postdoctoral research with Healthy Lake Huron partners; ABCA is the formal Mitacs partner. I am the postdoctoral scholar funded by the project.
- **Awarded support · 2024–2026:** Environment and Climate Change Canada project funding supported my PhD watershed and conservation research.
- **Professional practice (employee and consultant roles):** Proposal development and resource mobilisation at BRAC, ICCCAD and CARE Bangladesh, as a member or lead of proposal teams. Details are in the full CV.
- **OMAFA proposal — under review:** Contributed to a precision-conservation proposal led by Dr. Prasad Daggupati. The proposed work extends my PhD using the Agricultural Conservation Planning Framework (ACPF) to compare conservation opportunities, benefits, and costs. If accepted, I would work with the project team. [Proposal details →](collaboration.qmd#omafa-precision-conservation-proposal)
- **[Canada Postdoctoral Research Award (CPRA) program](https://nserc-crsng.canada.ca/en/funding-opportunity/canada-postdoctoral-research-award-program) — application submitted:** Proposed food-system resilience research; no award is confirmed. [Research direction →](collaboration.qmd#food-system-resilience-and-anticipatory-decision-making)
